chunks: From him, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān al-Kalbī, from al-Ḥalabī, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Do you know from where zina entered upon the people?” I said, “I do not know.” He said: “It came from the side of our khums, the khums of Ahl al-Bayt, except for our good and pure Shiʿah; for it is made halal for them and for their births.”

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the rightful recipients mentioned here
key_terms.الزِّنَا: fornication; mentioned here as entering among people through unlawful dealing
key_terms.الْأَطْيَبِينَ: the pure and good ones; describing the Shiʿah in this narration
key_terms.خُمُسِنَا: our khums; the one-fifth due belonging to Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.لِشِيعَتِنَا: for our Shiʿah; the followers of the Imams عليهم السلام
key_terms.لِمِيلَادِهِمْ: for their births; referring to the purity of lineage

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the permissibility of khums for the Shiʿah and its connection to pure lineage?
ai.summary: This hadith states that unlawful appropriation of the khums due to Ahl al-Bayt could lead people into zina-related impurity, while the Imams عليهم السلام made it halal for their pure Shiʿah during ghaybah. It highlights the legal and lineage-related significance of khums in Shia hadith tradition.
